{{short description|Award for expository papers in mathematics}}
{{notability|date=May 2019}}
The '''Merten M. Hasse Prize''' is awarded every two years by the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA) to recognize an exceptional expository paper appearing in an MAA publication, at least one of whose authors is a younger mathematician, generally under the age of forty. First awarded in 1987, the prize honors inspiring and dedicated teachers and encourages young mathematicians to take up the challenge of exposition and communication.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://maa.org/merten-m-hasse-prize/|title=Merten M. Hasse Prize - Mathematical Association of America|language=en|access-date=2024-11-10}}</ref>    

== Recipients ==
The recipients of the '''Merten M. Hasse Prize''' are:<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book|title=Recognizing excellence in the mathematical sciences : an international compilation of awards, prizes, and recipients|date=1997|publisher=JAI Press|others=Jaguszewski, Janice M.|isbn=978-0762302352|location=Greenwich, Conn.|oclc=37513025}}</ref>
* 2023: Matt Davis, Adam E. Parker, and Daniel A. N. Vargas
* 2021: Zvi Rosen, Jessica Sidman, and Louis Theran
* 2019: David Treeby
* 2017:  [[Lasse Rempe-Gillen]] and Zhaiming Shen<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2017-07/maoa-tmw072517.php|title=Top mathematics writers awarded prizes at MAA MathFest|website=EurekAlert!|language=en|access-date=2019-05-16}}</ref>
* 2015:  Charles Doran and Ursula Whitcher
* 2013:  Henryk Gerlach and Heiko von der Mosel
* 2011:  [[Alissa Crans|Alissa S. Crans]], Thomas M. Fiore, and Ramon Satyendra
* 2009:  Andrew Bashelor, Amy Ksir, and Will Traves
* 2007:  Franklin Mendivil
* 2005:  Maureen T. Carroll and Steven T. Dougherty
* 2003:  [[Manjul Bhargava]]
* 2001:  [[Francis Su|Francis Edward Su]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ccms.claremont.edu/content/Francis-Su-receives-MAA039s-Hasse-Prize|title=Professor Francis Su (HMC) receives MAA's Hasse Prize {{!}} Claremont Center for the Mathematical Sciences|website=ccms.claremont.edu|access-date=2019-05-16}}</ref>
* 1999:  Aleksandar Jurisic
* 1997:  Jonathan King<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Jackson|first=Allyn|date=1997|title=MAA Prizes Presented inAtlanta|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199711/comm-maaprizes.pdf|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|volume=44|pages=1473}}</ref>
* 1995:  [[Andrew Granville]]
* 1993:  [[David H. Bailey (mathematician)|David H. Bailey]],  [[Jonathan Borwein|Jonathan M. Borwein]], and [[Peter Borwein|Peter B. Borwein]]
* 1991:  [[Barry Arthur Cipra]]
* 1989:  Irl Bivens
* 1987:  Anthony Barcellos
